\caption{Odds ratios of flooding that the data exclude, from effects injected into the observed labels (exploratory; amendments 8 and 9). A: all ground nearest a water-related name; B: the part within 500\,m of the settlement; CA, CB: the same targets for truly water-related names, given the measured misreadings. Upper bound: the odds ratio at which the no-effect reference plus the mean injected gain reaches the upper 90\,\% limit of the observed increment, with that limit taken from the bootstrap of the primary analysis (base models fixed), with the spread over 13 assignments of location groups to folds added, or with the second stage refitted within each bootstrap replicate. Reference: reassigned names with rebuilt composition unless stated. Detectable: the odds ratio whose mean gain exceeds the reference by 2.80 standard errors of the increment (two-sided 5\,\%, power 80\,\%). Simulated odds ratios: 1.28, 1.65, 2.12, 2.72, 4.48, 7.39, 20.09; for A and CA also 1.05, 1.11, 1.16, 1.22 (amendment 9); 50 replicates per effect and target; values beyond them are marked $>$ or $<$. In parentheses: 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles over 2,000 resamples of the replicates (Monte Carlo interval); the resampling is drawn afresh for this table, so a limit can differ in the last digit from the same interval in Table~\ref{tab:eight-bounds}. Lower bounds: effects that set flooded labels to dry with probability $1-p'/p$, at odds ratios 0.78, 0.61, 0.47, 0.37, 0.22, 0.14, 0.05; the bound is the odds ratio below which the gain would exceed the same limit. Effects that differ between settlements: odds ratio $e^{\delta w_s}$ around settlement $s$ with weights $w_s$ drawn from an exponential distribution with mean one (50 replicates); bound and margin are read on the mean.}\label{tab:nine-bounds}
